materials.title: Getting ready for a walk
materials.text:
Choose the best reply in each conversation.

1. Parent: Are your shoes comfortable?
Child: ____

2. Child: This lace has come undone.
Parent: ____

3. Parent: Would you like the shorter route today?
Child: ____

4. Child: Where can we rest?
Parent: ____

5. Parent: Ready to walk again?
Child: ____

questions.prompt:
Parent: Are your shoes comfortable?
Child: ____
questions.explanation: A statement of fit answers comfort. Day/family/colour do not.

questions.prompt:
Child: This lace has come undone.
Parent: ____
options: Let’s stop here and tie it.
questions.explanation: Stopping to tie a lace addresses it. Books/taste/time do not.

questions.prompt:
Parent: Would you like the shorter route today?
Child: ____
options: Yes, please. My legs are tired.
questions.explanation: Accepting shorter route with fatigue reason fits. Ability/location/colour do not.

questions.prompt:
Child: Where can we rest?
Parent: ____
options: On the bench beside that tree.
questions.explanation: Bench gives rest location. Time/age/wheels do not answer where.

questions.prompt:
Parent: Ready to walk again?
Child: ____
questions.explanation: Readiness and improved condition answer. Object/travel/day count do not.

units.title: The cup behind the flowerpot
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: The cup behind the flowerpot
materials.text: Ella cannot find her small blue cup. She looks on the kitchen table and beside the sink, but it is not there. Her brother asks whether she took it into the garden. Ella remembers drinking water while drawing flowers. They go outside together. The cup is behind a flowerpot, where she put it to keep the paper dry. A tiny leaf has fallen inside. Ella takes the cup back to the kitchen and washes it before using it again. Her brother says the cup had a garden adventure. Ella writes a reminder beside her drawing: bring the things you need back inside.

questions.prompt: Ella is looking for a small blue cup.
questions.explanation: Opening identifies missing cup.

questions.prompt: The cup is beside the kitchen sink.
questions.explanation: She checks sink without finding it; actual place behind garden pot.

questions.prompt: Ella had been drawing flowers outside.
questions.explanation: She remembers drinking while drawing flowers in garden.

questions.prompt: A leaf is inside the cup when it is found.
questions.explanation: Tiny leaf has fallen inside.

questions.prompt: Ella drinks from it again before washing it.
questions.explanation: She washes before using again.

units.title: A bridge for the toy bus
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: A bridge for the toy bus
materials.text: Tom makes a paper bridge for his toy bus. He puts one end on a low box and the other on a stack of books. At first, the middle bends and the bus stops. His sister folds another sheet like a fan and puts it under the bridge. The folded paper helps support the middle. Tom tries again, and the bus crosses slowly. He does not put his feet on the little bridge; it is made for a toy. After playing, he keeps a drawing of the folds. The next day, he wants to try the same idea with a lighter model car.

questions.prompt: Tom makes the bridge for a toy bus.
questions.explanation: Opening states toy-bus purpose.

questions.prompt: The bridge works perfectly on the first attempt.
questions.explanation: Middle initially bends and bus stops.

questions.prompt: His sister adds folded paper underneath.
questions.explanation: Fan-like sheet supports middle.

questions.prompt: Tom stands on the paper bridge.
questions.explanation: Explicitly does not put feet on toy bridge.

questions.prompt: Tom plans to try a lighter model car next.
questions.explanation: Final sentence states next-day plan.

units.title: Grandpa’s little wooden spoon
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: Grandpa’s little wooden spoon
materials.text: Grandpa has a wooden spoon with a small flower on the handle. He uses it for stirring his tea. One day, Mia asks why he does not choose a shiny new spoon instead. Grandpa says her aunt painted the flower when she was young. The spoon reminds him of her first art class. Mia offers to paint a new one too, but Grandpa asks her to wait until they have suitable materials and a plan. They draw flowers on paper that afternoon. Mia chooses a purple flower for her drawing. The old spoon stays beside Grandpa’s cup, ready for tomorrow’s tea.

questions.prompt: The spoon has a flower on the handle.
questions.explanation: Flower handle detail explicit.

questions.prompt: Mia painted the old flower when she was young.
questions.explanation: Mia’s aunt painted it, not Mia.

questions.prompt: The spoon reminds Grandpa of an art class.
questions.explanation: Aunt’s first class connected memory.

questions.prompt: They paint the new spoon immediately that afternoon.
questions.explanation: Wait for suitable materials/plan; draw on paper instead.

questions.prompt: Mia draws a purple flower.
questions.explanation: Her drawing flower is purple.

units.title: Five places
units.instruction: Choose a suitable word from the shared bank for each gap.
units.alignmentNote: Complete five-gap fixed shared bank; new explicit contexts, no independent age calibration.

materials.title: Five places
materials.text: Shared bank: behind | between | in | on | under

questions.prompt: The tree is in front of Ben. Ben is ____ the tree.
questions.explanation: Behind is the opposite positional relation to in front of. Other prepositions do not express this reversal.

questions.prompt: The ball is ____ two boxes, with one box on each side.
questions.explanation: Between relates the specified two boxes. Other positions do not state one on each side.

questions.prompt: The cat is ____ the table; her tail comes out from beneath it.
questions.explanation: Beneath supplies the same location as under. Other candidates do not match it.

questions.prompt: The poster is fixed ____ the wall.
questions.explanation: On the wall is the attached surface. Other bank prepositions do not describe poster placement in this context.

questions.prompt: The key is ____ the closed box. Open the lid to get it.
questions.explanation: In locates key inside closed container. Other candidates do not require opening lid.

units.title: Five feelings
units.instruction: Choose a suitable word from the shared bank for each gap.
units.alignmentNote: Complete five-gap fixed shared bank; new explicit contexts, no independent age calibration.

materials.title: Five feelings
materials.text: Shared bank: cold | hot | hungry | thirsty | tired

questions.prompt: I have not eaten lunch. I feel ____ and want some food.
questions.explanation: Hungry concerns wanting food. Other feelings do not specifically name food need.

questions.prompt: I want a drink of water because I feel ____.
questions.explanation: Thirsty specifically names needing a drink. Other feelings may coexist but are not the stated need.

questions.prompt: This winter wind makes me feel ____. I need my warm coat.
questions.explanation: Cold and warm-coat need match. Hot opposite; hunger/thirst/fatigue different conditions.

questions.prompt: The room is too warm. I feel ____ and want to open a window.
questions.explanation: Hot follows excessive warmth. Cold opposite and other states not temperature.

questions.prompt: After the long walk, my legs feel ____ and need a rest.
questions.explanation: Tired specifically expresses fatigue and rest need. Other feelings not leg tiredness.

units.title: Five everyday forms
units.instruction: Choose a suitable word from the shared bank for each gap.
units.alignmentNote: Complete five-gap fixed shared bank; new explicit contexts, no independent age calibration.

materials.title: Five everyday forms
materials.text: Shared bank: are | can | has | have | is

questions.prompt: This ____ my red notebook.
questions.explanation: Singular this takes is. Are plural, has/have lack required object relation and can lacks main verb.

questions.prompt: These ____ our clean cups.
questions.explanation: Plural these takes are. Is singular, has/have/can do not form this identification.

questions.prompt: Maya ____ two sisters.
questions.explanation: Singular Maya has expresses possession. Have disagrees and be/modal forms do not state possession here.

questions.prompt: We ____ three spare pencils.
questions.explanation: Plural we have expresses possession. Has disagrees and other entries do not.

questions.prompt: I ____ swim, but my brother is still learning.
questions.explanation: Can takes base swim to express ability. Be/have forms do not directly precede bare swim this way.

units.title: A number on the thermostat
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: A number on the thermostat
materials.text:
A thermostat can display a temperature as a ____1____, but that figure may refer to the room's current temperature or to the temperature the user wants. Understanding which one is shown matters before deciding that the system is working incorrectly.

A ____2____ detects temperature at a particular point. The controller can use a ____3____ between the detected value and the desired one to determine a heating action. The exact behaviour depends on the equipment and how it has been arranged.

The system's ____4____ is not necessarily instant. Heat takes time to move through a room, and a displayed change does not mean every corner becomes warm ____5____. Turning a control repeatedly may therefore create confusion if the user expects the air to follow each movement at once.

A person may ____6____ the desired temperature, but the effect still depends on the building and heating system. The change in the room can be ____7____ rather than sudden. A number on a display is an instruction or observation within a process, not a magic description of everything in the room.

The device's ____8____ also matters. A reading near one source of warmth may differ from conditions elsewhere. That does not automatically prove the instrument is broken. It may show that one measurement point does not represent every place equally.

Useful controls combine readable information with a ____9____ relation between what users do and what the system does. Instructions should explain the relevant limits instead of relying on the user to guess. Knowing those limits helps people make a considered adjustment rather than operate the control ____10____.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Number is the displayed numerical temperature. Sensor is a component and comparison a relation, not the printed value.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Sensor detects temperature. Response/comparison/location do not name the detecting device.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Comparison between actual and desired values supports control. Response is subsequent action, not the relation between measurements.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Response is the heating system’s action or change. Number/location are not the temporal reaction described.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Immediately contrasts heat-transfer delay with an instant change. Blindly concerns information use, not elapsed time.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Adjust means change the desired setting. Borrow/whisper do not perform temperature selection.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Gradual contrasts with sudden. Tropical concerns a climate and decorative appearance, not pace of change.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Location names the measurement point. Comparison/response do not identify where the device is placed.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Reliable means dependable relation between action and result. Decorative/tropical do not describe functional consistency.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Blindly means acting without understanding feedback. Immediately concerns timing, not informed operation.

units.title: The work a typeface is asked to do
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: The work a typeface is asked to do
materials.text:
A typeface can be chosen for its personality, but a reading page also asks it to perform practical work. One concern is ____1____: whether individual letters and words can be recognised under the conditions in which they will be read. An attractive sample does not answer that question for every use.

Readers need to ____2____ similar forms. A design that looks elegant in a large heading may make some characters harder to tell apart in a small label. Size, spacing and the medium all contribute to the result.

The relevant ____3____ is therefore more than the font's name. A long printed essay, a moving display and a short interface label make different demands. Testing only a decorative title gives limited information about sustained reading.

Some ____4____ within the design can support recognition. If every form were made nearly identical for visual neatness, readers would lose useful differences. Consistency need not mean erasing every distinctive feature.

A page also uses type to establish a ____5____. Headings, notes and body text can signal different roles. The point is to make those relationships apparent, not simply multiply styles. Too many competing signals can make the structure less clear.

Design choices have ____6____ for different readers. A difficult page may discourage someone even when every sentence is technically present. It is unhelpful to assume that availability alone makes information equally ____7____ to everyone.

This does not require one universal typeface. It requires attention to use and a willingness to check an ____8____ against actual reading conditions. A choice can ____9____ the work's character while improving its practical clarity.

The result may be quiet: a reader follows the argument without stopping to admire the letters. Typography has supported the text ____10____ without becoming the subject of every glance. Its success is partly in making another activity possible.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Legibility concerns recognition of written forms. Hierarchy is structural ranking, context use conditions and unanimity agreement, not letter recognition.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Distinguish means tell similar forms apart. Erase removes differences and preserve retains rather than discriminates.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Context covers size/medium/task. Variation describes differences and hierarchy ranking, not the surrounding use setting.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Variation gives distinctive forms, contrasted with nearly identical letters. Unanimity is agreement among people, not visual differentiation.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Hierarchy assigns levels/roles to headings and text. Legibility concerns character recognition, not structural ranking.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Consequences are effects on readers. Other nouns do not name the outcomes of choices in this plural construction.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Accessible means usable by readers, not merely present. Edible concerns food and other entries lack adjective suitability here.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Assumption is a belief to test against conditions. Costume/unanimity do not name a provisional design belief.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Preserve retains character while improving clarity. Erase is the opposite; distinguish does not mean keep that character.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Visually specifies typography’s visual support. Privately concerns audience/secrecy, not the sensory medium.

units.title: A routine seen from the new member’s chair
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Write ONE word in each gap. Gap 0 is an example. Use capital letters; marking ignores case.
units.alignmentNote: Complete original eight-gap, one-word open cloze with fixed example 0. Recorded C1 sample is a task-format reference only; no C1 equivalence or independent learner calibration claimed.

materials.title: A routine seen from the new member’s chair
materials.text:
Changing a familiar routine (0) IS sometimes harder than writing a new set of instructions. As ____1____ turns out, people may have been relying on habits that nobody thought necessary to explain. The written plan can be clear while its practical meaning remains partly shared knowledge.

Our club discovered this when a new member asked where to leave completed work. It was not ____2____ we tried to answer that we noticed two different arrangements were being followed. Established members had each assumed their own habit was the common one.

The organiser asked us to describe the actual steps rather ____3____ defend our first explanation. We became aware ____4____ how many small decisions occurred between receiving a task and handing it over. A shelf label settled one question; it did not settle every other one.

Members needed time to get used ____5____ the revised routine. During a short trial, everyone recorded the point at which an instruction became unclear. When two labels contradicted each other, we had no choice ____6____ to decide which arrangement we intended to use.

The difficulty had nothing ____7____ do with the newcomers being unwilling to learn. They had made visible a gap that experienced members could cross on habit alone. After revision, a person could follow the sequence on ____8____ own without needing to know which unspoken custom belonged to which table. That was a more useful result than simply announcing that the instructions had always been obvious.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 1 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: As it turns out is the fixed introductory expression. That does not form it.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 2 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: Not until/till ... that marks the point discovery occurred. Since does not fit the delayed-discovery construction.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 3 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: Rather than contrasts describing with defending. Then is temporal.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 4 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: Aware of introduces the object of awareness. Aware to how does not fit.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 5 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: Get used to a routine takes to. For does not complete accustomed-to expression.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 6 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: No choice but/except to decide expresses the sole available action. Than does not form the construction.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 7 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: Nothing to do with is the established relation expression. For does not fit.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 8 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: A person may follow on their/his/her own with a possessive before own. Them is object form, not possessive.
